body: Conceptually `getWidgetRenderState` shouldn't trigger side effects when you call it—I'm wondering if those assignments should be in `init`?

It would be nice to have such a syntax:

```ts
connectorState.refine ??= page => { /* ... */ }
```
If I do that, then the tests which ran getRenderState before init (in index) seemed to fail. In some other cases we had moved it to getWidgetRenderState too. I'm not sure either what's the best
https://tc39.es/proposal-logical-assignment/#sec-assignment-operators, it's stage 4 so we can look into if it needs to be enabled for babel / ts
I just tried and it requires `@babel/plugin-proposal-logical-assignment-operators` to be added (as well as a new eslint rule, I guess) . I can create a separate PR with this if you want.
I think we can decide on that later

> getRenderState before init (in index) seemed to fail

Which makes sense because `init` is supposed to be called before `getRenderState` right now.

If we think long-term, when `init` doesn't exist anymore, it makes sense to manipulate `refine` _only_ in `getWidgetRenderState` (because it'll become contained in that method)—so I think it's fine to have this as it is now. But let's all be aware of this unexpected side effect.
that's what I thought too, if init doesn't exist anymore, getWidgetRenderState should be in control of the initialisation of functions which should only be set once.
